info.album: There's A Riot Goin' On (Expanded Edition)

podcast.body: Featured on the 1972 album "There's a Riot Goin' On," this song is explicitly not a disco record. It is characterized by a "muddy" sound, a muted guitar (in contrast to the typical front-and-center role in rock bands), and is notable for being the first pop song to use a drum machine as a central focal point, creating a "heartbeat" like rhythm. "family affair is muddy while the guitar was typically front and center and rock bands here the guitar is muted. But listen to what happens when the drum machine takes the center stage. Okay it it sounds like the heartbeat right that's the first time that a pop song used a drum machine in that way"

srcs.episode: FTR70 Sound Bite - Remembering Sly Stone

podcast.body: This 1971 song by Sly and the Family Stone featured pre-programmed rhythm sounds from a drum machine, indicative of the 1970s trend where artists experimented with such devices despite their limitations to preset patterns. "Then in 1971 we had Slime the Family Stone with Family Affair."
